explanations.answer: They will never walk in the darkness
explanations.explanation: Jesus says, “Whoever follows Me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.” No bulbs, no batteries, no feeling around the wall for a switch. Just following Him. I can tell you from my own years in the dark, that promise lands.

explanations.answer: They will never be hungry again
explanations.explanation: I'd love to hand out that promise with every cookie box, but it's not the one in this verse. Here Jesus is talking about light and darkness. Hunger comes up in another place, where He says, “Whoever comes to Me will never go hungry…” (John 6:35). Same Jesus, different promise.

explanations.answer: They will never be troubled again
explanations.explanation: Close neighborhood, wrong house, friend. In this verse the promise is about darkness and the light of life, and troubles aren't mentioned. Jesus does talk about troubled hearts at another time: “Do not let your hearts be troubled.” (John 14:1). Stick with the light here.

The Pharisees, strict religious leaders, say, “You are testifying about Yourself; Your testimony is not valid.” That's the whole complaint, right there. They've got one objection and they lead with it. Hold onto it, because Jesus answers it next.

explanations.answer: He is teaching on the Sabbath
explanations.explanation: The Sabbath doesn't come up in this passage. The Pharisees, strict religious leaders, aren't upset about the day or the schedule. They say He is testifying about Himself, and that His testimony is not valid.

explanations.answer: He never studied with a teacher
explanations.explanation: That complaint isn't in these verses, friend. The Pharisees, strict religious leaders, aim at one thing only: “You are testifying about Yourself; Your testimony is not valid.” Nobody here brings up His schooling.

Jesus doesn't agree with them. He says the opposite: “Even if I testify about Myself, My testimony is valid, because I know where I came from and where I am going.” They called it not valid, and He says it is valid. That's a hard no, said calmly.

Right, He doesn't agree. He answers, “Even if I testify about Myself, My testimony is valid, because I know where I came from and where I am going.” So the Pharisees say not valid, and Jesus says valid. He gives His reason right away and doesn't just stand there.
Jesus says, “I am not alone; I am with the Father who sent Me.” That's why His judgment is true. He's never standing there by Himself. A Father is who He points to.
Prophets are respected folks, but Jesus doesn't name them here. He says He is with the One who sent Him, and that One is the Father. Read the verse again and the blank fills itself.
Elders don't show up in this verse. Jesus says He isn't alone because He is with the Father who sent Him. He's not pointing to a panel of anybody.

Jesus says, “Even in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two men is valid.” Then He counts His two: He testifies about Himself, and the Father who sent Him also testifies about Him. He is using their own rulebook on them. Two is all it takes, and He's got them.
Seven would be a lot of witnesses to line up, friend. But the Law Jesus points to says two. He names His two right after: Himself, and the Father who sent Him.
Twelve is a whole crowd, and Jesus doesn't ask for one. He says the testimony of two men is valid. His two are Himself and the Father who sent Him.

They ask, “Where is Your Father?” and Jesus answers, “You do not know Me or My Father.” Then He adds, “If you knew Me, you would know My Father as well.” So the question gets an answer, just not the kind they were fishing for.

This one is true as written. The Pharisees ask where His Father is. Jesus answers, “You do not know Me or My Father. If you knew Me, you would know My Father as well.” That's exactly what the card says.

explanations.answer: His hour had not yet come
explanations.explanation: The text says it plainly: “…no one seized Him, because His hour had not yet come.” He's teaching in the open, near the treasury, and still nobody can grab Him. The timing isn't up to the crowd. It's up to His hour.

explanations.answer: The guards are afraid of Him
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say anyone is afraid, and no guards even come up here. It gives one reason: His hour had not yet come. I think it's easy to want a bigger reason, but the verse hands you the real one.
No feast rule is mentioned in this verse. John says no one seized Him because His hour had not yet come. That's the reason the text gives, so that's the one we keep.
Jesus says, “Where I am going, you cannot come.” This is one of the heavy parts, friend. I think it's worth slowing down on. The word is cannot, and Jesus says it straight.
I think that would be a gentler sentence, but it's not the one Jesus says. He says, “Where I am going, you cannot come.” This is a heavy part of the passage. The word is cannot.

Must sounds like a command to follow, but that's not what He says. Jesus says, “Where I am going, you cannot come.” It's a heavy line, and I think it should be read slowly. The word in the verse is cannot.
Jesus says, “…unless you believe that I am He, you will die in your sins.” Everything hangs on who He is. Believing it is what He asks. It's a serious word, so take it in slowly.
Abraham, Israel's forefather, doesn't come up in these verses. What Jesus says they must believe is “that I am He.” The question on the table is who Jesus is.

Moses, Israel's leader, isn't named in this passage. Jesus does mention “your own Law” earlier (John 8:17), but the belief He asks for here is different: “…unless you believe that I am He.” It all comes back to Him.

Nothing new comes out of that conversation. They ask, “Who are You?” and Jesus replies, “Just what I have been telling you from the beginning.” So He points back to what He's already said. No fresh announcement, friend.
Right, nothing brand new. When they ask, “Who are You?” Jesus answers, “Just what I have been telling you from the beginning.” He sends them back to what He's been saying all along.

John tells us, “They did not understand that He was telling them about the Father.” Jesus is speaking about the One who sent Him, and it sails right past them. Sometimes the answer is sitting right in front of you. I've done that with my own mustache.
This one is true as written. John says, “They did not understand that He was telling them about the Father.” He is talking about the One who sent Him, and they don't catch it.

explanations.answer: He does nothing on His own
explanations.explanation: Jesus says they will know “that I do nothing on My own, but speak exactly what the Father has taught Me.” Every word comes from the Father. He isn't freelancing. That ties right back to the One who sent Him.

explanations.answer: He learned it all from the scribes
explanations.explanation: The scribes aren't mentioned in this passage. Jesus says He speaks “exactly what the Father has taught Me.” His Teacher is the Father.

explanations.answer: He speaks only to His followers
explanations.explanation: That doesn't match what Jesus says earlier. In verse 26 He says, “…what I have heard from Him, I tell the world.” He isn't keeping it for a small circle. The world is who He's speaking to.
Jesus says, “…I always do what pleases Him.” Always, not once in a while. That's why He says the Father has not left Him alone. I'd love to hear that about my own batches, friend.
Surprises is a fun word, but it's not in the verse. Jesus says, “…I always do what pleases Him.” The word is pleases.
Worry doesn't show up in this verse. Jesus says the Father has not left Him alone, “because I always do what pleases Him.” The word that fits is pleases.
John closes the scene with “As Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him.” After all that back and forth, many believe. That's a good note to land on. Papa Dorin approves.
John doesn't say they walked away. He says, “As Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him.” Believing is what the text says.
No one asks for a sign in this verse. John says that as Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him. What happens here is belief.
